A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Clean-PR work. Their main text, tables, figures, algorithm, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including content relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original SWE-bench experiments, data-construction and augmentation ablations, and generalisation and sampling analyses in Tables 6–9 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds 7B, multilingual, OpenHands, and semantic leakage results in Tables 10–12 and 16.

M1.justification: The core filtering, Search/Replace conversion, mid-training, and stepwise SFT procedures remain unchanged. Section 3.4 adds an agent variant trained on 491 successful OpenHands trajectories and executed through multi-turn CodeActAgent, a limited procedural adaptation beyond the original Agentless pipeline.

E1.justification: v2 extends repository-repair evaluation beyond Python to Multi-SWE-bench Flash, covering C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Rust, and TypeScript. It adds multilingual SFT using Multi-SWE-bench-RL and training/evaluation involving interactive OpenHands trajectories. The original benchmarks and multilingual mid-training corpus remain.

E2.justification: The additional comparisons include SWE-Gym and Lingma-SWE-GPT at 7B in Table 10 and an OpenHands-specific comparison against Qwen-Instruct, SFT-only, and SWE-Gym in Table 12. These extend existing comparator families and controls; the original Tables 6–7 retain their membership. SWE-Swiss is discussed but not included in reported comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include 7B models, 300 multilingual test instances with 9,331 multilingual SFT samples, and OpenHands v0.28 CodeActAgent with a 100-turn limit and empty-patch, looping, and turn metrics. Appendix A.7 adds similarity-stratified evaluation. The original 32B training and Agentless settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled checks of transfer across model scale and inference frameworks, including agent failure diagnostics. Appendix A.7 newly investigates whether train-test similarity explains success, using similarity quintiles and manual inspection of the ten closest pairs. The original format, issue-linking, augmentation, forgetting, and sampling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.7 introduces a Pearson correlation and significance test between similarity and resolution outcome, reporting r = -0.061 and p = 0.184. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals for the main performance comparisons.

E6.justification: New results include 7B Pass@1 of 14.5%/20.4% on Lite/Verified, multilingual Pass@1 of 12.3%, OpenHands resolution of 20.7%/24.7%, and similarity-quintile outcomes. These are additional settings, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions. Original result tables remain unchanged; Section 3.2 corrects the SFT-only Lite value from 10.3% to 11.3%, matching Table 6 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical task formulations and Algorithm 1 are unchanged apart from presentation and spelling. v2 adds empirical similarity and correlation analysis, but no new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central corpus, training-pipeline, and original performance claims remain. The introduction and conclusion extend the demonstrated contribution to transfer across model scale, programming languages, and inference paradigms, whereas v1 left agentic and broader model evaluation largely to future work.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the additional results as evidence of transferable editing priors and particular benefits at limited model capacity, and interprets the leakage audit as supporting generalisation. Appendix D replaces the earlier untested-agent/single-scale discussion with an explicit limitation concerning broad edits excluded by the five-core-file filter, while retaining cross-architecture generalisation as future work.

D1.justification: v2 documents new study details, including multilingual training counts, OpenHands version and turn limit, and BGE-Code-v1 embeddings with FAISS IndexFlatIP. Existing hyperparameters and processing specifications remain. The contribution statement changes 'we release' to 'we plan to release'; both appendices already describe a future release, so an actual availability change cannot be established.

R1.justification: v2 adds SWE-Swiss as complementary work combining SFT, reinforcement learning, and self-consistency. It also adds references supporting the contamination analysis, code embeddings, and FAISS. The broader positioning around PR-based mid-training remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section hierarchy are retained. v2 adds Section 3.4, Appendix A.7, an appendix contents page, acknowledgments, and publication information; it locally rewrites the conclusion and discussion and corrects terminology and wording.

P2.justification: v2 adds four result tables covering scale, multilingual repair, agents, and similarity quintiles. Existing figures and tables retain their designs, with some relocation and renumbering; Algorithm 1 moves to the final page. These are localized additions and layout adjustments rather than a document-wide redesign.

improvement.justification: Section 3.4 substantially addresses v1's explicitly untested generality beyond a 32B model and Agentless inference, and tests multilingual repair rather than inferring it from multilingual training. Appendix A.7 adds evidence about contamination, while Appendix D states a concrete large-edit limitation. These changes strengthen the central argument's validity and applicability. The leakage audit does not prove contamination absent, and performance uncertainty remains unreported, but the overall evidential improvement is substantial.
